title: Living vs beatified: occult inspiration vs vision in the divine essence; distance no bar if God opens hearts
source_text: XLII. Caeterum, ex illius sensu, longe aliter viventibus absentia revelantur, atque Sanctis qui aeterna gloria fruuntur. Illis enim nota fiunt occulta inspiratione, his autem contemplatione divinae essentiae, in qua veluti in speculo res omnes & ab illis videntur, & sunt longe perfectius, quam in semetipsis existant. Addit non esse inconveniens, si fateamur Sanctos in coelis videre opera nostra in terris. Cum enim nulla corporis mole praepediantur, non impediri etiam locorum distantia, nec corporibus interjectis, quo minus preces nostras audiant, actiones intueantur, adeoque in cordibus nostris & cogitationibus illa videant, quae volumus ipsis esse manifesta. Quemadmodum enim sine externa voce, aut sensibili signo, Angeli tum sibi mutuo, tum animabus loquuntur, & vicissim ab illis audiuntur, & intelliguntur: ita homines sola voluntate sua spiritibus tam bonis, quam malis, interna desideria & cogitationes aperire posse, & ab illis intelligi, non obstante corpore quo vestiuntur, vel quavis loci intercapedine, tametsi magna. Nolentium vero cogitationem, & mentem nemini patere praeter unum Deum, qui solus scrutatur corda & renes, & cui voluerit Deus revelare. Cap. 12. de Veneratione Sanctorum in explicatione propositionis secundae.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover, in his sense, absent things are revealed far otherwise to the living than to the Saints who enjoy eternal glory. To the former they become known by hidden inspiration; to the latter by contemplation of the divine essence, in which, as in a mirror, all things both are seen by them and exist far more perfectly than they exist in themselves. He adds that it is not inconvenient if we confess that the Saints in heaven see our works on earth. For since they are hindered by no bulk of body, they are not hindered even by distance of places, nor by bodies interposed, from hearing our prayers, beholding our actions, and even seeing in our hearts and thoughts those things which we wish to be manifest to them. For just as without external voice or sensible sign Angels speak both mutually and to souls, and in turn are heard and understood by them: so men by their will alone can open inward desires and thoughts to spirits both good and evil, and be understood by them, notwithstanding the body with which they are clothed, or any interval of place, however great. But the thought and mind of those who are unwilling lie open to no one except the one God, who alone searches hearts and reins, and to whom God has willed to reveal. Cap. 12. on the Veneration of the Saints in the explanation of the second proposition.
pass_b_english: Living learn hidden things by occult inspiration; the beatified see them in God’s essence as in a mirror—more perfectly than in themselves.
No bodily bulk or distance bars Saints from prayers, acts, and opened thoughts.
Unwilling minds stay closed except to God alone, who searches hearts.

lemmas.gloss: by contemplation of the divine essence

choices.why: Classic beatific-vision image for knowing creatures in God.
